topic: 6 strange borders countdown ending on India's vanished enclaves, with Baarle-Hertog and Baarle-Nassau at number two
hook: Your front door can be in Belgium while your kitchen is in the Netherlands, and India has a border even stranger.
title: Your Door in 2 Countries: 6 Borders, 1 in India
description:
Six real borders that make no sense, from a house in Baarle where the front door decides the country, to the Indian enclaves in Bangladesh that vanished from the map at midnight in 2015. Each stop is a real place you can find on a map, and each one is stranger than the last. Watch to the end for India's strangest border, then tell us which one you would live on.

#borders #geography #india
comment_prompt: Which border would you live on?

scenes.narration: Your front door can be in Belgium while your kitchen is in the Netherlands, and India has a border even stranger.
scenes.headline: ONE HOUSE, TWO COUNTRIES

scenes.narration: Six real borders, each stranger than the last. At the end, a whole set of borders disappears at midnight.
scenes.headline: 6 BORDERS, 1 COUNTDOWN

scenes.narration: Every border here is real, and all but one still sit on the map today.
scenes.headline: ALL REAL

scenes.narration: We start small, with a village that is German on paper but surrounded by Swiss land on every side.
scenes.headline: WE START SMALL

scenes.narration: And keep watching, because the last border on this list is the one that ended one of the strangest maps on Earth.
scenes.headline: INDIA IS LAST

scenes.narration: These borders are not accidents. Each one exists because of an old treaty, a king, or a deal.
scenes.headline: NOT ACCIDENTS

scenes.narration: Number six: Büsingen. Look at your map and you will find a German village wrapped completely inside Switzerland.
scenes.headline: BÜSINGEN

scenes.narration: It sits on the northern bank of the Rhine river, right next to the Swiss city of Schaffhausen.
scenes.headline: ON THE RHINE

scenes.narration: Everyone there lives under German law, yet the shops take Swiss francs and many locals work across the line in Switzerland.
scenes.headline: SWISS MONEY

scenes.narration: Cars from this village carry the letters BÜS on the number plate, a code you will not find anywhere else in Germany.
scenes.headline: THE BÜS PLATE

scenes.narration: Walk a few minutes in any direction and you leave Germany, but you never reach the rest of Germany.
scenes.headline: AN ISLAND OF GERMANY

scenes.narration: To get to another German town, you have to cross Swiss land first. The village is an island without any sea.
scenes.headline: ISLAND WITH NO SEA

scenes.narration: The whole village sits inside the Swiss customs area, so trade rules there follow Switzerland, not Germany.
scenes.headline: SWISS CUSTOMS AREA

scenes.narration: In 1918, the villagers voted to join Switzerland. The deal never happened, and the village stayed German.
scenes.headline: THEY VOTED TO LEAVE

scenes.narration: Imagine paying for your chai in Swiss francs, in a village that officially belongs to Germany.
scenes.headline: CHAI IN FRANCS

scenes.narration: So one street mixes a German address, Swiss money and Swiss customs rules. Strange, but still fairly calm.
scenes.headline: A MIXED-UP STREET

scenes.narration: Number five exists because of one word in an old treaty. Meet Llívia, a Spanish town inside France.
scenes.headline: LLÍVIA

scenes.narration: In 1659, Spain and France signed the Treaty of the Pyrenees. Spain gave a group of villages to France.
scenes.headline: TREATY OF 1659

scenes.narration: But Llívia was officially a town, not a village. So the treaty's words did not cover it.
scenes.headline: TOWN, NOT VILLAGE

scenes.narration: That one word kept Llívia Spanish, while the new border was drawn all around it. It is still Spanish today.
scenes.headline: ONE WORD SAVED IT

scenes.narration: Look at the map and you see a small patch of Spain, sitting inside France, with no Spanish land touching it.
scenes.headline: SPAIN INSIDE FRANCE

scenes.narration: A short road links Llívia to Spain. It crosses French land, but travellers are allowed to use it.
scenes.headline: THE ROAD HOME

scenes.narration: Walk the streets and you see Spanish flags, Catalan signs and Spanish shops, with France waiting just outside town.
scenes.headline: SPANISH STREETS

scenes.narration: Think about that: more than three hundred years ago, one word saved a town from changing countries, and it still matters today.
scenes.headline: STILL MATTERS TODAY

scenes.narration: Remember this idea of a place cut off from its own country. Number one is the biggest version of it.
scenes.headline: REMEMBER THIS

scenes.narration: Number four: Point Roberts, an American town that you can only reach by land through Canada.
scenes.headline: POINT ROBERTS

scenes.narration: In 1846, a treaty set the US-Canada border along the 49th parallel, a straight line of latitude across the map.
scenes.headline: THE 49TH PARALLEL

scenes.narration: That straight line cut through the tip of a small peninsula, and the southern tip landed on the American side.
scenes.headline: THE LINE CUT IT OFF

scenes.narration: So Point Roberts is part of Washington state, but it hangs off the coast of Canada, with no road to America.
scenes.headline: AMERICA, ATTACHED TO CANADA

scenes.narration: To drive to the rest of the United States, you must enter Canada first, then cross into America again.
scenes.headline: TWO BORDER CROSSINGS

scenes.narration: The nearest big city is Vancouver, in Canada, not any city in the state it belongs to.
scenes.headline: VANCOUVER IS CLOSER

scenes.narration: Imagine a village that belongs to Kerala, but you can only reach it by driving through Tamil Nadu.
scenes.headline: IMAGINE IT IN INDIA

scenes.narration: If you enjoy strange places like these, subscribe to the channel. There is a lot more like this coming.
scenes.headline: MORE STRANGE PLACES

scenes.narration: Back to the map. A line drawn on paper in 1846 still decides how people on this peninsula live today.
scenes.headline: A LINE ON PAPER

scenes.narration: Number three: Campione d'Italia, an Italian town on the shore of a Swiss lake, hidden inside Switzerland.
scenes.headline: CAMPIONE D'ITALIA

scenes.narration: It sits on Lake Lugano, and Swiss land surrounds it on all sides except the lake.
scenes.headline: ON LAKE LUGANO

scenes.narration: To drive from Campione to the rest of Italy, you have to pass through Switzerland.
scenes.headline: ITALY VIA SWITZERLAND

scenes.narration: How did it happen? Centuries ago, the land belonged to a monastery in Milan, and it stayed Italian as Switzerland grew.
scenes.headline: A MONASTERY'S LAND

scenes.narration: Today, the town is part of the Swiss customs area, and people there pay in Swiss francs.
scenes.headline: SWISS FRANCS

scenes.narration: It is an Italian town with Italian people, Swiss money and Swiss mountains rising right behind the houses.
scenes.headline: ITALIAN TOWN, SWISS MOUNTAINS

scenes.narration: So you can eat Italian food, pay in Swiss money, and still be in Italy.
scenes.headline: PIZZA IN FRANCS

scenes.narration: So far, every border had a reason: a river, a word, a monastery. Now the line cuts through people's homes.
scenes.headline: NOW IT CUTS HOMES

scenes.narration: Number two: Baarle. Two towns, Baarle-Hertog in Belgium and Baarle-Nassau in the Netherlands, tangled together like spaghetti.
scenes.headline: BAARLE

scenes.narration: Walk down the street and you will see white crosses painted on the pavement. Each one marks the border.
scenes.headline: WHITE CROSSES

scenes.narration: The line runs through streets, gardens and houses. Step over a cross and you change countries.
scenes.headline: STEP, NEW COUNTRY

scenes.narration: Belgium owns little islands of land inside the Netherlands, and some of those islands hold Dutch islands inside them.
scenes.headline: ISLANDS IN ISLANDS

scenes.narration: That means a Dutch patch inside a Belgian patch inside Dutch land. Try drawing that on a map.
scenes.headline: TRY DRAWING IT

scenes.narration: It goes back centuries to land deals between local lords, long before Belgium and the Netherlands were countries.
scenes.headline: A MEDIEVAL DEAL

scenes.narration: Some buildings have the border running right through them, with one room in Belgium and the next in the Netherlands.
scenes.headline: BORDER THROUGH THE ROOM

scenes.narration: In 1995, the two countries agreed on a simple rule for houses: the front door decides which country the house belongs to.
scenes.headline: THE FRONT DOOR RULE

scenes.narration: So a kitchen can cross the line, yet the whole house counts as the country of its front door.
scenes.headline: KITCHEN IN ANOTHER COUNTRY

scenes.narration: Many houses show a flag or number plate near the door, so visitors know which country they are in.
scenes.headline: FLAGS BY THE DOOR

scenes.narration: Neighbours on the same street can follow different national rules, such as shop opening hours.
scenes.headline: DIFFERENT RULES, SAME STREET

scenes.narration: Two towns, two sets of rules, and tourists take photos with one foot in each country.
scenes.headline: ONE FOOT EACH SIDE

scenes.narration: You would think nothing beats that. But number one is a set of borders that vanished at midnight on 31 July 2015.
scenes.headline: VANISHED AT MIDNIGHT

scenes.narration: Number one: India's strangest border. For decades, India and Bangladesh held small islands of each other's land, deep inside their territory.
scenes.headline: INDIA'S STRANGEST

scenes.narration: They were called enclaves, or chhitmahals, and there were 162 of them in total.
scenes.headline: 162 ENCLAVES

scenes.narration: 111 of them were Indian land inside Bangladesh, and 51 were Bangladeshi land inside India, mostly around Cooch Behar in West Bengal.
scenes.headline: 111 AND 51

scenes.narration: Which side you lived on decided everything: your school, your vote and your hospital.
scenes.headline: YOUR SIDE DECIDED ALL

scenes.narration: Some were so small that a single field was foreign land. Step across its edge and you had left your country.
scenes.headline: A FIELD, A COUNTRY

scenes.narration: Dahala Khagrabari was an Indian patch, inside a Bangladeshi patch, inside an Indian patch, inside Bangladesh.
scenes.headline: DAHALA KHAGRABARI
scenes.sub: a country inside a country inside a country

scenes.narration: Draw it on paper and it looks like Russian nesting dolls, each country sitting inside the other.
scenes.headline: NESTING DOLLS

scenes.narration: One legend says it began with a chess game between two kings, who bet villages on the board.
scenes.headline: A CHESS-GAME LEGEND

scenes.narration: Historians say the real cause was old land deals and treaties, and then Partition in 1947 froze the pieces in place.
scenes.headline: FROZEN BY PARTITION

scenes.narration: Imagine living there. Your own country's police, school and hospital are on the other side of a border you cannot legally cross.
scenes.headline: CUT OFF FROM HOME

scenes.narration: Reports say many people there had little access to roads, power, schools or health care.
scenes.headline: LITTLE ACCESS

scenes.narration: Then at midnight on 31 July 2015, India and Bangladesh swapped the enclaves under a historic land agreement.
scenes.headline: THE GREAT SWAP

scenes.narration: The 51 Bangladeshi pieces became Indian land, and the 111 Indian pieces became Bangladeshi land.
scenes.headline: 51 IN, 111 OUT

scenes.narration: Residents were allowed to choose their country. Some stayed where they were and changed nationality overnight, others moved.
scenes.headline: THEY CHOSE A COUNTRY

scenes.narration: For thousands of people, that midnight finally gave them a country on their own doorstep.
scenes.headline: A COUNTRY AT LAST

scenes.narration: That is why India's strangest border is the one that no longer exists. Those 162 pieces are gone from the map.
scenes.headline: ERASED FROM THE MAP

scenes.narration: So here are all six: Büsingen, Llívia, Point Roberts, Campione, Baarle, and the Indian enclaves.
scenes.headline: ALL SIX

scenes.narration: And remember how this started: your front door can sit in Belgium while your kitchen is in the Netherlands. In Baarle, that is true.
scenes.headline: THE DOOR DECIDES

scenes.narration: Tomorrow: time zones that make no sense, including a country that sets its clocks 15 minutes off from its neighbour.
scenes.headline: TOMORROW: STRANGE TIME ZONES
